text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel says Turkey's claim to full membership of European Union cannot be realised but instead the customs union accord can be improved.
- Traffic police will introduce new regulations to decrease high level of vehicle accidents.
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan preparing a report to convince the military he cannot reform education as part of anti-Islamist measures wanted by the generals.
- More than 50 mobile phones a minute were sold in Turkey in the first three months of 1997.
- Parliament to vote on probe into alleged links between Erbakan's Islamist Welfare Party and a shadowy financier.
- The Turkish intelligence service MIT has uncovered no evidence about the murder of secularist journalist Ugur Mumcu in the 50 months since he was killed by a car bomb.
- Decree on the importation regime for 1997 has been agreed by the coalition partners after 82 days of delay.
- Turkey will build a paper factory to produce 40,000 tonnes of paper annually in Turkmenistan.
